verdict.rationale: Adyen's docs describe a client-side integration. The server calls /sessions and Adyen sends payment data to "your client-side application", with support for web, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter. Checkout styling is customizable and the payment form can be localized, and a client key authorizes allowed origins for client-side use. Together these imply payment UI embedded in the merchant's own site or app. missing for 10: explicit documentation of embeddable payment components (e.g. named UI components or a drop-in), an explicit statement that payments complete in-page rather than on a redirected hosted page, depth on what can be customized, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed customizable payment components directly in my own site or app instead of redirecting to a hosted page

citations.quote: Adyen sends payment data from our server to your client-side application.
Support online payments for web, iOS, Android, React Native, or Flutter.
Customize the styling of your checkout. Present your payment form in the local language of your shoppers with our localization support.
A single key for all your allowed origins in an environment.
